defence.sileris.harden.note: the coating hardens this long after the apply line ('You apply a sileris berry' or 'a quicksilver droplet to yourself'). 6 of the 49 applies printed no hardening line before the next apply or the log's end (az 3616; Z5 1891, 4096, 4712, 4951, 5284). A hit before the 10 s mark does not explain it: 36 of the 43 that hardened took a bite or a FLAY in that time too. Slickness at the mark does: rule defence.sileris.slickness_harden. The engine does not re-apply the coating; a fork reads an apply with no hardening line yet as the coating on its way (tools/theorycraft.py, review R3-fork-8). tools/test_kb_rules.py re-measures it
defence.sileris.harden.source: kb/sim/events.json streams: sileris.apply to the next sileris.up, before the next apply, in the four logs (az 12, Z5 9, g 7, X 15); first pair az 24 -> 10 s later

defence.sileris.slickness.note: 8 of 8 slickness gains in a packet that starts with the coating up printed 'The protective covering coating your skin sloughs off.' in the same packet (X 144-146: the second venom, 'You have been afflicted with slickness.', then the slough line). No slickness with the coating up left it on. All 8 are DSTABs. The engine strips it on a DSTAB, a give or a FLAY's venom and prints sileris.down (tools/sim/attackers.lua); the give and the FLAY are by analogy, no log shows them. A BITE lands only with the coating down. Review R4-engine-1. tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

defence.sileris.slickness_harden.note: 0 of the 43 applies that hardened had slickness on at the apply + 10 s (10 of them took slickness in the wait, and it was cured before the mark). 5 of the 6 applies that never hardened had it on (az 3616; Z5 4096, 4712, 4951, 5284). The sixth, Z5 1891, had slickness cured at +9.90 (row 2308) and a new apply in that packet (row 2310). The engine raises no coating at the mark when slickness is on (tools/sim/fight.lua timed). tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

alt: normal: the median +/- 3 sd (three uniform draws), held inside min and max
draw.shape.note: the shape of a drawn clock; --median takes the median and draws nothing, except in a fork: there a clock already running (a channel down at the row, a FLAY of the shield, a smoke for rebounding, an apply of the coating) takes the median of the part of its spread above the time already run, and that part rests on this shape (review R3-engine-2). The --seeds runs of a --median page draw too. A log's min and max are often a lost line or a slowing affliction (clock.rebounding: 0.026 and 250.253 around a median of 8.49; clock.focus max 4.992 against p90 2.542), so a tail never reaches them unless they lie within one width. --clock-draw normal runs the alternative
draw.shape.value: quantiles: linear between lo, p10, median, p90 and hi, 10% of the draws in each tail; lo and hi are one p10-p90 width past p10 and p90, held inside min and max
